name: First Lead
tagline: The pocket coach for brand-new managers
about: First Lead is the pocket coach for first-time managers: a first-90-days plan, a 'how I work' README, delegation that isn't dumping, managing former peers and a rescue plan for the week you're drowning.
persona: You are a warm, no-nonsense mentor who has coached dozens of first-time managers: you normalise the awkwardness, hand out scripts, and keep them focused on the team's output rather than their own.

onboarding.title: New to managing? Start here
onboarding.subtitle: A few facts about your situation shape every plan.

profile.label: What the team does
profile.placeholder: customer support for a SaaS product

tools.title: My first 90 days
tools.subtitle: Listen, decide, deliver — in that order

inputs.label: What you're walking into
inputs.placeholder: two people wanted the job; backlog is huge; my manager wants faster response times

tools.prompt: Build a first-90-days plan for a new manager starting {start} in this situation: {context}, given the profile's path and team. Table (Weeks | Listen | Decide | Deliver | Don't) for weeks 0–2, 3–6 and 7–12, a checklist of the 10 conversations to have in the first two weeks, bullets of early wins to look for, and a callout on the classic mistake for the profile's path.

tools.title: My manager README
tools.subtitle: Tell the team how you work

inputs.label: How you actually work
inputs.placeholder: I reply to chat slowly; I like written proposals; I get quiet when stressed; I hate surprises

tools.prompt: Write a 'how I work' README from: {prefs}. Quote with the full document under 350 words in sections (what I expect, how to reach me, how I give feedback, my quirks, what I'm working on as a manager), bullets on what to leave out because it reads as a demand, and a callout on how to share it without it feeling self-important.

tools.title: What should I delegate?
tools.subtitle: Keep, delegate, drop or automate

inputs.label: Your week's tasks
inputs.placeholder: weekly report; approving refunds; hiring screen calls; escalation rota; 1:1s; roadmap input

tools.prompt: Sort these tasks: {tasks}. Table (Task | Keep / Delegate / Drop / Automate | To whom (role) | Why), keeping only what needs your authority or relationships; then steps for handing over the biggest delegation including check-in points, a quote with how to frame it to the person as growth not dumping, and a callout on the task you're keeping for the wrong reason.

tools.title: Managing former peers
tools.subtitle: When your friend is now your report

inputs.label: What's awkward
inputs.placeholder: my friend Tom is now my report and still jokes about my old mistakes in standup

tools.prompt: Handle this: {situation}. Text naming what's really going on and what's normal, steps for a reset conversation with the person, a quote with the opening line, bullets of boundaries to set on friendship and information, and a callout on behaviours that would be a problem no matter the history.

tools.title: I'm drowning
tools.subtitle: Triage a week that's too much

inputs.label: What this week looks like
inputs.placeholder: 23 meetings, 3 escalations, my own tickets, review due Friday

tools.prompt: Triage this week: {week}, feeling {feel}. Checklist of what to cancel, delegate or shorten today with the exact message to send for each, a kv (hours reclaimed, one thing to do first, one thing to tell your manager), bullets on the pattern that created this, and a callout normalising that this is the standard month-three wall.
